cases.scenario: A support declaration claims only core but its summary says all transformation tests passed.
Check the commerce library with all implementation modules absent and network/database calls instrumented to fail if invoked.
Require plan.output for an interface-only component with no supported implementation.
A draft schema accepts a missing mandatory output while the normative requirement rejects it; qualification must stop.
A layered map declares datasets, products, policies and a recipe but no component or design; `check` and `catalog` with a DCAT export complete without any component, design, binding or fixture.

Known gap: a run record names its DocSpec job instead of a declared component or design. Until DocSpec job definitions are accepted as production declarations, the run cannot attach and assembly fails.
The catalog command is given --locked, or --lock with a path. It verifies no earlier lock, so it refuses the option as invalid usage and writes no output.

A project without components or designs declares a DocSpec job whose steps each name their recipe. A bounded run of that job names it as its production, and its output versions carry the run's inputs, time and outcome.
A job step's SQL differs by one byte from the recipe its step mapping names.
A run names the job, but its pinned request reorders two steps. Only input bindings and scratch paths may differ, so the run stays unbound.
Register two different component documents with the same URI identity and version through different aliases.
An interface-only reader passes declared output checks; inspect that evidence never becomes inferred or executed.
Parse JSON containing duplicate year keys; for a YAML implementation also exercise aliases, merge keys, and implicit date scalars.
An ODCS document combines two valid quality operators: the pinned corrected schema accepts it; the release comparison records its different result.
Add an unknown top-level component property named retryMagic; separately confirm a default annotation does not supply a required year.
Compare boolean true against numeric 1 and compare a decimal bound immediately above an exact decimal value.
An imported shared component and the root both declare orders; the imported component must bind its local dataset while /orders selects the root.
Project a imports b, which imports a; retain the import path in the failure.
Select a schema object name matching two objects, then separately verify that an exact stable ID takes precedence.
A required local property definition points to a missing file; a separate fixture forms a two-file definition cycle.
Check one imported project while a second known consumer project is excluded; the report must list uncovered consumers.
Remove all implementation references from the commerce components while retaining valid interfaces and dataset declarations.
Call a two-input transformation with orders supplied and customers absent, plus a separate unknown port extra.
Pass a literal object containing a parameter-looking key; its contents remain literal and null stays distinct from missing.
Omit required year even though its schema has default 2026.
A symbolic integer source admits 1999..2026 while the target admits 2000..2100; include finite-enum and exclusive-bound subcases.
Symbolic arguments participate in an unsupported whole-object conditional even though each individual primitive type matches.
Remove the customer_id column from an available dataset while the consumer lists that column with required false.
A nullable customer_id is supplied to a non-null input; enum labels match but their underlying allowed values do not.
A consumer requires physical decimal precision and a time-zone rule absent from the supported mapping.
Declare customer_id unique without testing rows; evidence must retain a declared assumption only.
One field is incompatible and another has an unknown physical type; the dataset comparison fails and retains both details.
Two named steps consume one another; a separate fixture references a nonexistent output port.
A design has two exports: one is correct and one omits an expected field; both receive results.
An opaque component has a declared output and no implementation; core can pass while a separately required inferred-output check is not run.
A missing producer blocks a dependent export, while an independent invalid argument is still reported.
Request an unrecognized URI-named policy rule with a valid extension-rule shape.
A rowIdentity annotation contains region twice and names a missing order_day field.
A SQL quality rule has no complete fieldDependencies metadata; separate cases declare a nonexistent field and valid dependencies.
A vocabulary policy selects /status with value retired while only draft and active are allowed.
A registered quality-bearing property definition has no consumers; warn without claiming the inherited rule was executed.
An invalid prerequisite must not be replaced by an empty object; independent documents still finish checking.
Select one design and require core.calls; include all its prerequisites and report excluded sibling consumers.

A layered map without components or designs lists only core.documents, core.references, core.datasets and core.policies. It passes, and its report requests neither core.graph nor core.calls. With a component declared, the same omission still runs both groups as required.
Many designs use the same file and definition; instrumentation records one parse per real path and byte digest.
Change component bytes but retain its URI identity and version in the candidate snapshot.
Rename reader argument year to fiscal-year; all three loaded designs are affected and their stale calls fail with dependency paths.
A candidate adds a required reader argument and weakens a promised output; distinguish input and output compatibility directions.
An override weakens minLength from 5 to 2; a separate unsupported custom restriction remains unknown and external consumers remain uncovered.
Two development builds share version 0.1.4 but have different source commits and wheel digests; their inventories must differ.
Change one followed shared-definition byte after locking; verification fails without rewriting the lock.
A saved plan uses a staged-file list; changing one file invalidates reused execution evidence even when the newest filename stays the same.
Repeat a locked check with shuffled discovery order; stable results match while timestamps remain in volatile metadata.
Attempt a required unsupported physical-type comparison; the instance is unknown with reason, evidence level, and applicability.
Reduce a report with a required failure and a required unknown; failed wins. Additional table cases cover optional failures and operational errors.
Hide all error messages in human rendering; the underlying failed results and exit code remain unchanged.
A report has declared, inferred, and executed checks; snapshot and missing-capability evidence remain separately visible.
A result uses a diagnostic code already assigned another meaning; release qualification rejects the reassignment.
Invoke check without execution flags while reader implementations contain deliberate import-time side effects.
Exercise malformed content, unreadable file, missing adapter, valid project, and invalid arguments; verify codes 1, 3, 2, 0, and 64 respectively.
Run JSON format with progress enabled and an invalid call; stdout is one valid failed report and progress is on stderr.
Request a two-export build when only one export is supported; no partial bundle replaces the previous successful bundle.
Discover a valid manifest next to an executable module that raises on import; a core inventory reads only the manifest.
Translate a dataset with unique keys and decimal precision while the target only preserves names and primitive types.
An ODCS backend cannot execute a requested custom quality rule; native lint success does not make that data check pass.
Configure a dlt discard policy without a quarantine writer; the receipt records available discard counts but no quarantine claim.
Compile a supported component, save plan bytes, consume them with explicit bindings, and retain input/output field order and type mappings.
The consumer accepts a plan but the standalone validator reports unresolved validity in loose mode; required standard validity is unknown.
An output has one duplicate row that a set comparison would erase; multiset comparison fails against independently expected rows.
A custom function declaration has no runtime implementation; requesting its execution cannot treat the declaration as executable code.
Interrupt a bundle build after generating one output; preserve the prior successful bundle and expose missing obligations.
Supply a reader output through a binding; mark the reader as injected, verify digests, and reject a duplicate origin binding.
A definition path or symlink resolves outside caller-permitted roots; no outside file or remote URL is read.
Arguments contain shell substitution text and an explicit secret parameter; values are passed structurally and reports redact the secret.
Exceed the configured artifact or reference-depth limit; retain partial diagnostics and return an operational error.

Cancel a fixture caller wait; retain configured failure evidence and original native operation identity. Remove only runner-owned temporary data after ownership is established. Do not infer native cancellation or remove protected candidates.
Supply a component with an unsupported mandatory DDK version even though its own artifact version is a valid SemVer.
An optional URI-keyed annotation is unknown; preserve it without changing core behavior or loading an adapter.
A first product release has passing offline, catalog, and SQL checks but has no executed saved Substrait fixture. Require the full first release profile set.
A fixture expected output was generated by the transformation under test; qualification rejects it as independent expectation evidence.
A release reports documentation-schema checks as runtime conformance results; qualification rejects the unsupported claim.
A release evidence bundle lacks exact dependency versions, unresolved checks, and fixture provenance.
An inherited pattern plus inline maxLength must preserve both restrictions for the selected resolver; compare release 1.2.9 and pinned main.

cases.scenario: Retain two original occurrences with equal content digests and different capture contexts. The catalog preserves both occurrences, their shared content reference, and the exact definition and source bindings.
Load contradictory observed values from the same authority for one version and scope. Report a conflict and retain the cited origins.
Resolve the commerce ODPS ports through the pinned schema and explicit selections of separate objects in one ODCS contract.
Resolve an ODPS port whose contract and version identify multiple registered objects but whose explicit object binding is missing.
Bind an ODPS port to the correct logical dataset at the wrong ODCS definition version.
Import an opaque externally assigned version and a separate byte digest. Preserve their native scheme and authority and resolve the representation against the same exact version.
Preserve a nested list element path and a literal field name containing a dot. Check the intended nested endpoint and accept a valid semantic self-relation.
Resolve a release-local virtual row position against a different release.
Validate a relationship that requires a two-part dated key but supplies only the document number.
Load valid check evidence for an older output under a different rule version. The current required check remains unresolved.
Attach a successful run receipt and a required check with no execution evidence. Keep discovery available and qualification incomplete.
Refresh from unchanged metadata in a fresh process. Reuse evidence at its original assurance level. Verify zero data-payload opens, copies or repeated checks and byte-identical outputs.
Move the publisher selection to a new release. An existing release-local binding and historical run continue to resolve the original inputs.
Display a valid empty published table, an unknown expected population, a confirmed absence, and an acquisition failure with distinct observations and access facts.
Require a catalog export whose adapter is missing. Preserve the prior complete output set and report the missing capability.
Generate a public catalog with a disclosure policy. Restrict private locations and evidence while retaining permitted version identifiers and public links.
Parse the generated DCAT JSON-LD with an independent reader. Navigate catalog, dataset, version and available distribution or service. Verify the current-version link against the cited selection.
Request discovery for a historical version with no advertised access. Preserve the version description and omit an available distribution.

Validate the job and observed run events and supported version facets against pinned schemas. Import the native and DDK events into one receiver, replay both, and verify that the same job, run, and physical datasets keep their original identities. Resolve the recorded input and output versions to exact native references.
Load only a declared job and a native run with an unresolved terminal outcome. Emit the declared job and supported observed events, and keep terminal coverage unresolved.
Change a loaded relationship and required quality rule while keeping the data and production definition fixed. Report affected consumers, required requalification and regenerated metadata.
Request assurance that all consumers were checked while one known consumer project is outside the loaded scope.

Build a catalog from definitions alone with no metadata adapter. Expose meanings, declared relationships and query examples. Keep availability and observed lineage unresolved and create no inferred current selection.

Build from a recipe whose authoring path is relative to the declaring document. Move the complete output set to an unrelated directory and remove access to the original project. Resolve the generated recipe locally and check that its SQL bytes match the original digest. Its checked use binds the requested exact input versions.

Load distinct public and preview selections for the same dataset plus a disjoint public selection for another dataset. Select the public authority and purpose and verify the two intended current versions. With no selector, emit no current links.

Select an authority and purpose for which two distinct current release records overlap on the same dataset. Reverse file order and vary observation times. Report ambiguity in either order and preserve the prior completed output set.

Read a terminal run with a partial input list and one separately retained source with no consumption evidence. Emit only the observed consumed version and keep the scope and partial coverage in DDK. Do not turn the unproven source into a run input.

Check a composite comparison with a small scalar fixture and independently expected matches and non-matches. Include a different calendar date, a padded textual key, unequal binary bytes, and each supported null policy. Verify the shared rule preserves types and exact values.
Load a valid versioned project rule and request a required check of its comparison. The evaluator is unavailable. Retain the relationship declaration and report the check as unknown.

Execute the local commerce workflow on independently authored inputs and expected rows. Check the design and one definition change; execute SQL and replay saved Substrait bytes through DocSpec; attach supported ODCS checks and OpenLineage to the exact saved-plan output. Resolve ODPS and DCAT and use the generated catalog to bind a checked query to that output. Include separate nested/scoped-identity cases; reject wrong versions, incomplete keys and missing evidence. Verify unchanged metadata refresh with no data-payload reads. Claimed intake uses the exact staged files; managed quality gates have their separate typed-operation acceptance.

Catalog generation and saved Substrait fixtures pass separately, but no reader binds a checked query through the generated catalog to the exact checked output of the same saved plan. The connected local demonstration remains incomplete.
Assemble once, count one read of each recipe SQL source, retain its exact bytes and all requested standard outputs, and verify that the atomic writer uses those retained bytes.
A required check is unknown. Return admitted definitions and companions with their unchanged check status, no publishable controls, and the previous complete output intact.
A contextual relationship does not resolve. Refuse structural admission and return neither catalog nor companion bytes.
Retain a recipe title, ordered notes, explicit positional parameter order, and resolved contextual relationships. Preserve actual query inputs without adding contextual endpoints.

Disclose selected nested and list field paths with necessary ancestors, types and nullability. Withhold unlisted siblings, native properties and the original private root object name; retain explicit partial-path scope.

Retain root and imported project extensions separately with exact declaring identities and namespace. Public extension access requires the exact source revision and explicit extension namespace grant.

The same virtual field supports a row-position identity and an additional unique key with identical path, type and scope. Resolve it once without inventing a physical ODCS property or losing the original key.
Two virtual declarations of one path disagree about type or scope. Refuse the relationship and catalog admission.

Load an external target without treating it as a local alias or fetching it. Retain the relationship, local import scope and unknown shared comparison; a required comparison keeps the build incomplete.

Changing recipe documentation or contextual endpoint meaning requires metadata and reader review. Actual input and production changes retain their stronger computation obligations; rule changes require qualification separately.
Change one scoped opaque project extension. Record the metadata change and unresolved domain impact without inventing a computation dependency.
An explicitly supplied profile establishes declaration support for fixed-width native byte keys while preserving ordered composite components and leaving observed matches and qualification absent.
A fixture-owned profile interprets exact versioned text-to-integer and list-overlap declarations from resolved ordered key definitions. DDK supplies no application rule names or data observations.
Support external digest-and-suffix reference construction while retaining the external namespace, not_assessed existence, and no version, run or qualification evidence.
Unsupported exact rule versions, rule identities, native types and external meanings remain required unknown outcomes with an admitted catalog but no complete output set.
A release-local virtual key used outside its release scope fails before the application profile can override the shared guard.
Untyped, malformed, unsupported-status or empty-reason profile results remain required unknown results and cannot generate a complete output set.
Capture the explicit profile source once per assembly, preserve its original digest and tool identity in catalog and lock, and accept an exact distribution pin without discovering source.
Refuse a public catalog whose selected profile ID is a private file URI without an explicit identifier grant; retain a safe public report, local provenance and the previous complete output.
An empty disclosure-only field path grants root descriptions only when descriptions are enabled, without exposing children, native properties or custom metadata.

Changed profile provenance or declaration assessments require metadata and reader checks only along actually assessed relationships. Preserve unresolved domain effects, unused profiles and relationships outside the snapshot without claiming computation reuse.
Reject incoherent profile provenance, mismatched assessment identities, unsupported assessment status or invented external existence during impact comparison.

Compare two actual generated public catalogs after a selected profile revision or source change. Retain permitted identity and redacted source, withhold private assessments and reasons, and preserve unknown assessment/consumer scope without fabricated reader dependencies.

Explicit physical-type grants with complete modeled-subtree disclosure preserve the exact native string, including native-only names. Declared objects and arrays remain composite without modeled children; nested permissions preserve only their admitted type values.

Complete logical field disclosure without explicit opaque-type permission still withholds composite native text. Root metadata grants reveal no root native type, while existing scalar disclosure remains exact.

A missing or hidden dataset, absent or blank type, invalid or root path, or incomplete modeled-subtree permission refuses public disclosure. A partial field grant plus a composite type grant preserves the previous complete output set.

Return private full metadata and the public view from the same captured source and one metadata read. Later source changes or private result mutations cannot change public metadata or make it disagree with the retained artifact bytes.

An unresolved required qualification keeps admitted private metadata available while public artifacts remain unavailable and the report incomplete. A separate structural failure leaves both catalogs absent.

Correct and explicitly delete keys against an exact selected source-only local base. Preserve unaffected rows and the protected base, recover after caller loss, refuse incomplete or wrong-candidate quality, and reuse computation after a rule-only change. Historical retries after a successor and lifecycle compaction return the original result without selecting it again.
Apply explicit null replacement and coalescing policies independently, then qualify a successful empty replacement scope. Preserve the native distinction between null, empty and missing work.

Advance the selected source composition after preparing and qualifying an Update. Native selection refuses the stale base, retains the newer selected result, and DDK reports the selection refusal separately from completed execution.

Lose the acceptance response and remove caller-owned evidence files. Reconcile the original accepted native evidence through selection and lifecycle compaction. Existing protection retains promised replay until explicit operation/result retirement; later payload removal leaves audit metadata without granting it a new retention promise.

Lose the first retained-job prepare or native action response. Repeated inspection keeps one pinned original request and compares every prepare field or supplied native request/candidate identity. A self-consistent receipt for different work remains unverified and cannot supply an observed candidate. Independent subprocess simulations isolate this transport boundary from native execution qualification.

After a confirmed retained-job selection, lose a later response or refuse a mismatched select retry. Keep the original selected outcome, candidate and accepted qualification as historical facts while recording the new command uncertainty or refusal separately.

A native request acknowledgment succeeds but says computation is admitted and not started. Preserve execution pending separately from the successful acknowledgment; do not invent running work, outputs, a candidate or accepted qualification.

Execute two independently authored inputs through a materialized join and aggregate, two retained exports, two blocking reports and a separate multirow metadata report. Compare duplicate, null, unmatched and integer results with independent expected rows. Native acceptance, rule-only requalification, missing caller artifacts and lost selection acknowledgment preserve the exact completed candidate and original identity.

Complete the same independent whole job with one deliberately nonzero blocking counter. Native qualification refuses while completed outputs, original candidate and factual execution remain available; selection stays pending and no accepted qualification exists.

Lose a managed request response after a child starts through pipe, selector, wait or cleanup failure. Keep the original request, dataset and native operation ID; report unknown execution and operational failure without inventing a child exit or replacing the primary cause. Every process wait remains finite.

Map exact retained native metadata into an actual catalog with complete scoped membership, original request bytes, captured definitions and deterministic controls. Open no payload or caller JobSpec; preserve private members in their native record and unknown row-consumption coverage.

Refuse changed candidates, incomplete native output/report membership, altered original bytes, caller pass booleans and resealed acceptance with wrong checks, evaluator, semantics or retained input pins.
Require every native input and output to have exactly one catalog mapping or explicit out-of-catalog reason; refuse omitted, overlapping or unknown members.
Retain completed native computation when accepted qualification is absent. Keep required quality unknown, expose no publishable artifacts and preserve previously written controls.
An admitted pending job can retain known sealed outputs without claiming a completed or qualified candidate.
Retain known outputs and unresolved qualification when native execution is unknown or failed; preserve the native failed outcome separately from missing quality evidence.

Changed authored constraints, production identity or original definition custody cannot inherit old native acceptance, even if effective schema bytes remain equal. Do not attach the old run to the current production.
Known output field, type or membership mismatches fail schema interpretation even when the separate native policy passed.
Preserve supported nested field positions, dictionary strings, exact fixed binary width and explicit timestamp semantics in output-schema interpretation.
Unsupported authored meanings and unmatched value constraints remain unknown. Nullable nested observations preserve compatible schema facts while leaving required row properties unresolved.

Use an explicitly supplied generator and original JobSpec to bind authored required, ordered key uniqueness and key nonnull facets to exact accepted report counters. Preserve nullable schema observations and open no payload or caller JobSpec.
Wrong writer, SQL, field, counter, original job, source or profile and missing, duplicate or unauthored bindings cannot qualify authored facets. Callback inputs remain immutable.
Retain authored primary-key obligations independently of an alternate catalog key. Missing or duplicate primary positions remain unresolved rather than disappearing behind the alternate key.

Public native facet claims retain the explicitly granted generator identity separately from the native evaluator. Source locations require an evidence grant; private native members and diagnostics remain withheld.
A public native facet claim without an explicit generator identifier grant refuses disclosure and produces safe public diagnostics.

An exact supported native export can establish uniqueness only for the entire visible ordered key. Same-output schema and accepted required-field facts separately establish every component of a nonnull key.

A hidden additional sort field, mismatched runtime or settings, or missing nonnull evidence prevents full key qualification. Unique larger tuples never prove a visible key subset unique; uniqueness alone never proves nonnull.
A declared row_position supplies its complete same-release key even when physical keys also exist, without a duplicate virtual key declaration or fabricated executed uniqueness evidence.
A row_position identity cannot authorize a version-pair relationship outside its same-release scope.

Nested authored primary keys inside objects and list elements remain required unknown until their scoped native interpretation is supported; nullable schema metadata and an unrelated accepted policy cannot erase them.
The original native policy ID cannot acquire different original policy bytes or accepted authority conditions, even when metadata witnesses are coherently resealed.
A distinct native requalification policy ID may retain the original prepare request while binding a new policy and authority pair. Do not require original and requalified policies to be equal.

Version 2 native-table metadata preserves the original selector, exact requested metadata pin, original member locations and native owner without opening payloads. This is an offline consistency check, not proof of native execution or protection.
Coherently resealed version 2 metadata refuses mixed witness versions, missing or conflicting snapshot pins, overlapping file bindings and an unsupported passed-boolean prerequisite.

The complete candidate and its view set must both contain the same typed snapshot custody. Missing copies, boolean integers and integral decimal tokens cannot replace native integer selectors or sizes.

Coherently resealed custody metadata refuses invalid roles, order, duplicate locations, foreign ownership, sizes, digests, original-operation identity and contradictory empty or selected-snapshot membership. Native seals remain responsible for actual closure completeness.

An explicitly empty selected snapshot retains only its original metadata. Preserve an earlier origin_operation identity in authored metadata without claiming native cross-operation reuse was executed.

Seed a bounded native table through its public CLI and consume the exact selected snapshot through DDK managed_job. Independent expected values, nulls and native field IDs match; original member locations, hashes, sizes and retained bytes remain exact. A diagnostic count stays separate from required zero counters before acceptance and selection.

Remove the fixture payload before native admission completes and require failure without a candidate. Restore those exact payload bytes, remove original metadata and manifests, then retry the original operation through a cold DDK adapter. Actual output reading succeeds. Later remove all producer and caller originals and replay the same accepted candidate before selection.

An incorrect original metadata SHA, table UUID, schema ID or selected snapshot must produce the concrete native identity or pin refusal through DDK. Coherently update JobSpec and policy pins so unrelated artifact mismatches cannot satisfy the check. No candidate, accepted qualification or output is produced.

Complete native input references preserve opaque admission digests, lifecycle record identities, logical name rebinding and original-copy operation provenance. Both witnesses and the receipt bind the same current inputs; no payload is opened and metadata does not establish fresh native custody.

Coherently resealed current input references refuse another scheme, owner, operation, request, input ordinal or lifecycle table incarnation, invalid native integers and changed digest algorithms. All current references must identify one lifecycle table and UUID.

Current input references require complete matching witnesses and exact receipt membership/order. Refuse mixed legacy/new inputs, unbound or duplicate handles, mismatched copies and decimal substitutions. Historical completed candidates cannot acquire unbound references.

A requested reuse_from requires an exact source grant in both complete witnesses and a current input reference. Refuse missing, unrequested, changed, foreign-owner or conflicting lifecycle-table grants. File-only version 1 evidence cannot gain snapshot custody handles.

Native handles on pending, unknown or failed operations remain unresolved metadata. They create no catalog input-version binding, accepted qualification or published artifacts; input coverage stays explicitly unknown.

Map completed version 2 native-table observations to exact catalog-only references. Preserve every original selector and metadata-pin value, literal locations and null snapshot meaning; keep retention and consumption unknown and add no available representation.

Observe one exact source through different aliases, operations, retained copies and schema observations. Keep one source version with separate receipt owners, and retain per-run schema and custody evidence outside the source-version key.
Retain earlier unpinned native-table selectors in their original evidence without promoting them into exact version 2 catalog identities or claiming availability.

Generate deterministic catalog and standards observations for exact native-table inputs. Preserve public withholding, opaque lineage identity and discovery without an invented native reader or access distribution.

Pass a native-issued same-owner input custody reference through two later managed operations, including a renamed input. Remove the original producer and donor caller JobSpec/policy before receiving preparation. Preserve original object identities, bytes, original-copy operation, independent rows, nulls and native field IDs. Native acceptance and cold replay after receiving caller-file loss preserve candidate, reports and accepted qualification before selection.

Change the lifecycle table incarnation, opaque admission digest or donor input name on an otherwise retained native custody reference. Require the exact managed_job_identity refusal and no candidate, accepted qualification or selection; preserve unknown execution and selection observations instead of claiming that no work ran.

Bind version 3 producer evidence to exact original request, adoption, native custody and retained evidence bytes without opening artifacts. Preserve distinct file inputs, adopted prerequisite order and current JobSpec order; validate actual catalog shapes, assembly and public withholding.
Refuse invalid native adoption identities, nil table UUIDs, and integral decimal tokens in any independently resealed identity copy, including evidence references and prerequisite candidates.

Refuse conflicting completion/view/request/body bindings, unknown evidence roles, changed fixed policy identity, missing current custody or changed native evidence bytes. Inline witness consistency does not establish native producer qualification.

Refuse missing, duplicated or changed model prerequisites, wrong proof candidates, incomplete input scope, aliased or unrelated proof custody, and producer record submissions in the model role. Native resolves actual accepted proof authority.

Refuse proof metadata claiming model selection or exports, missing original producer records, and producer authority added to earlier completion profiles. Preserve native execution as a separate untested capability.

Accept an original-record proof, refuse selecting the proof itself, and use its exact native custody in the fixed model. Remove original producer and caller artifacts, interrupt the model after admission with a missing declared file, then recover under the same request after restoring those exact bytes. Verify independently authored rows, nulls, native field IDs, original custody, accepted qualification and cold replay before model selection.

A completed original-record proof reports a nonzero required counter and a positive informational count. Require exact job_report_failed refusal while preserving its candidate; a model naming an invented acceptance must then receive producer_prerequisite_unaccepted without accepted qualification or selection.

Supply correctly pinned original record bytes whose producer commit is outside the adopted inventory, then remove the source payload. Require producer_record_mismatch before payload copy, with no observed candidate, accepted qualification or selection. A refusal does not establish that nothing executed.

Use an actually accepted proof but change a model file's bytes and request pins outside the adopted file inventory, then remove that file. Require producer_file_inventory_mismatch before file opening, with no observed model candidate, accepted qualification or selection.

Present an actual accepted unbound candidate as the model's prerequisite. Require producer_prerequisite_mismatch rather than treating a real but unrelated acceptance as the adopted proof; observe no model candidate, accepted qualification or selection.

Use an actual accepted proof and a valid model policy document that removes one of the two fixed required reports under the same policy ID. Remove the model file and require producer_policy_mismatch before file opening, with no observed model candidate, accepted qualification or selection.

A verifier-confirmed accepted producer proof has complete zero-export membership and matches its captured definitions. Admit a deterministic ordinary locked catalog with the exact source version and proof run, preserving private withholding and unknown current availability. Add no output versions, field-rule passes, release or selection claims.

The complete zero-export proof lacks native acceptance, or the caller explicitly requests dataset qualification without version-bound obligations. Preserve required not_run evidence and withhold the locked output set.

A zero-export accepted proof names a captured production or source definition that differs from the current authored definitions. Preserve required unknown status, omit the current production link and withhold the locked output set.
Exclude every exported output of a legacy or model job from the catalog. Preserve the required unknown scope result; an omitted model output is not a known zero-export proof.

A verified local native publication-intent receipt preserves its exact producing job, native table incarnation and saved generation. Record retained or retired payload state separately from computation, selection and external publication. Fresh unbound inspection may establish explicit absence. These independently authored metadata and subprocess simulations do not qualify native execution.

Lose the first freeze response and preserve the complete pinned request. Require exact replay before bound inspection can confirm that proposal. Refuse changed requests, crossed operation kinds and altered or decimal-normalized pinned evidence before another submission. These independently authored metadata and subprocess simulations do not qualify native execution.

After a verified saved decision, a failed, absent, conflicting or unconfirmed refresh preserves historical identity with current payload state unknown. An exact retired payload generation cannot become retained again. These independently authored metadata and subprocess simulations do not qualify native execution.

Quarantine malformed or mismatched native publication metadata, including invalid enum shapes, integer tokens, table incarnation, candidate, original job identity, inline byte pins, inventory and external-effect claims. A conflicting refusal protocol remains unknown. These independently authored metadata and subprocess simulations do not qualify native execution.

Near-limit native stdout remains recoverable through a compact receipt at the same capture and metadata limits. Oversized original requests and pre-submission cancellation launch no process. An oversized final recovery record returns no success and preserves original request and raw reply. Prior decoded payloads have no consumer after their audit is verified. These independently authored metadata and subprocess simulations do not qualify native execution.

The publicationIntent report variant permits no computation, selection, data outputs or job-qualification claims. Success and absence require pinned observations; unknown requires a reason. Existing bounded and managed job branches retain their prior requirements. These independently authored metadata and subprocess simulations do not qualify native execution.

Through the actual public DDK adapter and native CLI, lose the first freeze response, remove caller controls, recover the exact intent and control/pointer bytes, select a newer job, and replay the original intent. Retire its exact native payload generation, compact, and preserve the original audit through cold inspect and replay. Local fixture only; external authorization and dispatch remain not_run.

Through the actual public DDK adapter, refuse changed epoch, accepted qualification, row inventory and colliding pointer with exact native refusal codes. Each refused initial freeze leaves explicit not_found. After a valid freeze, a changed inventory refuses and inspection returns the unchanged saved decision. Local fixture only; no provider publication claim.

Compose independent selectors, exact schema IPC, adoption, current proof custody and accepted prerequisite from verified accepted version 3 proof metadata without artifact opens. Preserve proof observation order separately from explicitly supplied unique complete adopted prerequisite order. Refuse unverified, unaccepted, earlier-profile or model evidence and ambiguous/incomplete input scope. Receiving authority and local model inputs remain caller-owned; DocSpec independently resolves native admission.
A disclosed complete release retains its exact version membership and selection while withholding the ungranted private native reference; a separate explicit native-reference grant retains it.
Omitting a release member from public disclosure changes complete membership to partial and never upgrades an already partial or unknown scope.
A paired consumer refuses altered release identity, membership, completeness, native reference, selection authority, purpose, release, observation time or current selection.
Local version and release observations with withheld native references refuse before public disclosure; only public output can replace an admitted exact reference with a withheld marker.

A protected version observation preserves the original logical VersionRef and Arrow schema while retaining the native physical selector and stored metadata byte pin. Empty snapshots remain null. Legacy omitted observations supply no producer pin. No metadata or payload opens or retained parser-cache entries occur during validation.

Malformed physical metadata, invalid physical-selector integer tokens, ambiguous or incomplete native input membership and normalized URI spellings cannot produce an admitted observation. Preserve raw evidence under unverifiedResult and return unknown without nativeReads. Logical VersionRef identity checks retain their separate report outcome.

Through the actual native runtime, preserve independently authored nested values, native field IDs and exact protected versions. Compare physical selector and stored-byte identity, repeat from a cold adapter and refuse corrupt metadata and unavailable or mismatched versions. Metadata observation supplies no later custody or acceptance.

An explicit private snapshot-source configuration path changes only the native command prefix. Preserve the original job request, operation and accepted evidence; do not open the source configuration or add it to public receipts. After response loss, source-free inspection recovers the same original intent. The option cannot enable an unsupported job owner. Independent subprocess simulations establish transport behavior only.

A supervising application explicitly keeps structured DocSpec requests and protected reads in its owned POSIX process group. TERM and KILL of that group stop an adapter-launched harmless native stand-in and preserve the original recorded request. Standalone placement stays the default; adapter timeout stops and reaps the direct child while retaining unknown execution and the original operation ID. A protected read can explicitly override inherited placement. Process probes establish transport containment only, not native completion or rollback.
An aggregator root with no artifacts imports four layers that also import their lower neighbours; each project loads once at its shortest import path and longer paths resolve as recorded aliases.
A project declares neither artifacts nor imports.
One import path reaches a copy of a layer project with the same identity and version but different bytes.
One import path reaches an identical copy of a layer project in another directory, whose relative artifact paths could resolve differently.
Two layers imported directly by the root also import each other, so both cyclic occurrences are aliases; the cycle is still reported with its file chain.
A layer-order rule over a flat aggregator root checks product ports, relationships, recipe inputs and production inputs, all pointing to the same or a lower layer.
Separately, a capture product port, a source relationship, a source recipe input and a capture component input point to higher layers.
The product namespace is left out of every layer while its ports and recipe still depend on lower layers.
A layer names a namespace that is not loaded, or a namespace already assigned to another layer.
A property's definition-type link points to a remote glossary URL or host path while the contract does not opt into inlining; inline values stand and no remote resolution is reported.
The contract opts into inlining with the DDK inlineReferences annotation and a property links to a remote definition document.
Assemble the layered map with DCAT; each dataset, product, relationship and recipe appears once, references through aliases bind canonical datasets, and the details record the import aliases.
Product records carry the ODPS name, type, domain, status, description and context exactly as authored.

Dataset records carry attribution, contract status, object description, tags and context, and a contract block with description, context, tags, canonical URL and only the SLA entries that apply to the object.
An SLA entry names an element in an external file that DDK cannot interpret.
A public view keeps product type and status and dataset status and attribution, withholds free text without a descriptions grant, and keeps canonical URLs only when granted as locations.
A granted project extension names its own withheld namespace; granting that name as an alias admits the extension unchanged.
A view-sources rule selects the source namespace; its view property names a stored sibling in transformSourceObjects and gives transformLogic.
Within the rule's scope a view reads a missing property or another view, or omits transformLogic.
A resolved dataset outside the rule lists an upstream object in transformSourceObjects and passes; selecting that dataset in the rule makes it fail.
A view-sources rule names a namespace that is not loaded.
A retained original declares a derived or model origin, or a dataset names an unknown origin.
A layer registers an artifact with the same alias as its aliased import; the artifact and the imported namespace both still resolve.
A row-identity rule targets an object that declares its key only with ODCS primaryKey and primaryKeyPosition.
A row-identity rule targets an object with no key, or with two primary-key properties at the same position.
SLA entries name the object by schema path, a property path, a mixed list, another object, a differently cased name, or only through the deprecated default element.
A public view with descriptions receives SLA entries naming a private field, entry links and custom properties, and verified statements with custom properties.
Granted extension values embed a withheld alias inside a path or name a withheld ODCS object name; a granted identifier and plain words pass.
Recipes join declared inputs, read object fields and unnested array elements, bind ?, $n and :name parameters, and produce exactly the columns and types of their declared result dataset.
A recipe reads a table that is not one of its inputs, a schema-qualified table, or a non-recursive CTE from inside its own body.
A recipe reads an undeclared column, object field, or array-element field, reads a field of a string or indexes one, joins USING a missing column, or orders by a missing ordinal.

A recipe mixes type families in a comparison, IN list or subquery, BETWEEN, IS DISTINCT FROM, CASE branches or UNION columns, compares a date with a non-ISO string, applies LIKE to a number or arithmetic to a string, or binds positional parameters in parse-tree rather than text order.
A recipe uses more positional parameters than parameterOrder names.
A view's declared properties add a column and change a type that its recipe output does not match, or declare a nested object field type its recipe does not produce.
A recipe calls a function outside the parser profile and its signature table, extracts JSON with an operator, or names a dialect without a parser profile.

A datafusion recipe calls regexp_match, regexp_like, the json_get family, make_array, unnest, array_length and to_date with argument types DataFusion 53.1 accepts. Each call is typed from the pinned signature table, and the output matches the declared result dataset.

A datafusion recipe passes a number to regexp_like, a string to array_has or unnest, a fractional JSON path, or the wrong number of arguments to regexp_match, or mixes number and string elements in make_array or array_has.
One projection of a datafusion recipe repeats an alias, or an identical unaliased expression in a UNION ALL branch. DataFusion refuses both.
catalog.recipes is requested without a tool environment; separately it is not requested.
